title: Ordinary Brown representability for levelwise quasi-coherent module systems
statement: Fix universes containing all sites, diagram indices, Hom sets and coproduct indices below [def-weil-size-convention]. For any scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal C_T=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ denote the full subcategory of the ordinary unbounded derived category of structure-module sheaves with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category, pqf-def-coherent]. Also allow the following second kind of category. Let $T_\bullet$ be a small semisimplicial diagram of schemes whose transition module pullbacks are exact. Use their small Zariski ringed sites and the ringed total module category $\mathscr M$ and exact evaluations $e_n$ of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. Let $\mathscr A\subset\mathscr M$ be the full category of systems whose components are quasi-coherent modules; no invertibility of their transitions is required. Write $\mathcal C_{T_\bullet}=D_{\mathscr A}(\mathscr M)$ for the full subcategory of $D(\mathscr M)$ consisting of objects $E$ for which every $H^q(e_nE)$ is quasi-coherent. The categories $\mathscr M$ and $\mathscr A$ are Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], $\mathscr A$ is closed under coproducts, and kernels, cokernels and extensions of its objects computed in $\mathscr M$ remain in $\mathscr A$. The ordinary derived categories $\mathcal C_T$ and $\mathcal C_{T_\bullet}$ have set-indexed coproducts computed by termwise sheaf coproducts. For either choice $\mathcal C$, every exact functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ to a locally small triangulated category with set-indexed coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-category] that preserves those coproducts has an ordinary right adjoint. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of the schemes, and no boundedness of the complexes, is required.

source.place: Tag 077P, proposition-coherator, part (1), for Grothendieck abelianness of QCoh on arbitrary schemes. Hall--Neeman--Rydh, One positive and two negative results for derived categories of algebraic stacks, arXiv:1405.1888v2, Appendix A Theorem A.3 and Appendix B Theorem B.1, read at https://arxiv.org/html/1405.1888 (archive WANTED); Brown for well-generated categories as in Hall--Rydh, Perfect complexes on algebraic stacks, Theorem 4.14(1), proof citing Neeman Proposition 1.20. For the total-system specialization, use exact free evaluation adjoints of spaces-simplicial.tex Tag 0D72: their values on sets of QCoh generators generate the levelwise category. This is an ordinary weak-Serre Brown theorem, not a theorem about cartesian sections or gluing adjoints.

proof.text: For each scheme $X$, use the Grothendieck categories $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ and a generator of each. The latter inclusion creates small colimits. It contains zero since $0=\widetilde 0$ on every affine open. The kernel, cokernel, extension and arbitrary-coproduct results cited here show that this is a weak-Serre subcategory closed under coproducts. This verifies all underived hypotheses for the single-scheme case without a finiteness assumption on $X$.

For the semisimplicial diagram, pullback preserves quasi-coherence and is left adjoint to module pushforward. It therefore preserves small colimits: maps from the pulled-back colimit correspond, by adjunction, to compatible families of maps from the pulled-back diagram. The same holds on the quasi-coherent full subcategories because their colimits are created in module sheaves. By hypothesis these pullbacks are exact. Apply the existing free-evaluation adjunction $\ell_p\dashv e_p$, whose component formula is $e_m\ell_pG=\bigoplus_{\alpha:[p]\hookrightarrow[m]}f_\alpha^*G$. It restricts to the levelwise quasi-coherent systems by the pullback and coproduct closure just cited. Thus these systems are ordinary lax systems, with the same adjunction formula; no transition is inverted.

In both system categories, form kernels, cokernels and colimits componentwise. Exactness of transition pullbacks induces the kernel transitions, and preservation of colimits induces the cokernel and colimit transitions; the universal properties hold componentwise. In particular both categories are abelian, and evaluation detects exactness. The componentwise kernels and cokernels remain quasi-coherent by the cited closure results. For a filtered diagram of short exact sequences, evaluating its colimit gives the colimit short exact sequence in the corresponding Grothendieck component category. Hence filtered colimits in both system categories are exact. If $G_p$ is a generator of the $p$th component category, then $G=\bigoplus_{p\geq0}\ell_pG_p$ is a generator: a nonzero system morphism $h:E\to E'$ has a nonzero component $h_p$, so faithfulness of $\operatorname{Hom}(G_p,-)$ gives $u:G_p\to E_p$ with $h_pu\ne0$. Its adjunct $\ell_pG_p\to E$, extended by zero on the other summands, detects $h$. The sum is small by the size convention. Apply this argument once with all modules and once with quasi-coherent modules. This proves that $\mathscr M$ and $\mathscr A$ are Grothendieck abelian.

source.place: 0D72 free-evaluation formula; properties.tex 077P component generators; agent-supplied AB5 and generator argument

proof.text: Evaluation is exact. Therefore a kernel or cokernel of a map between objects of $\mathscr A$ lies in $\mathscr A$ by the corresponding component result; an extension of two objects of $\mathscr A$ lies there by the component extension result. Coproducts lie there by component coproduct closure. Thus $\mathscr A$ is a full replete weak-Serre subcategory of $\mathscr M$ closed under small coproducts. Apply the abstract representability result to $(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)=(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_T),\operatorname{QCoh}(T))$ and to $(\mathscr M,\mathscr A)$. Exact evaluation gives $e_nH^q(E)=H^q(e_nE)$, so its second derived subcategory is exactly the one in the statement. In both cases it supplies the ordinary triangulated category, its ambient termwise coproducts, and cohomological representability.

source.place: Appendix A Theorem A.3 and the localizing-subcategory observation following it

proof.text: Fix $d\in\mathcal D$. The functor $H_d(c)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(Fc,d)$ takes values in abelian groups in the fixed Hom universe. Exactness of $F$ and the triangulated Hom exactness axiom make $H_d$ cohomological; preservation of coproducts by $F$ and their universal property give $H_d(\bigoplus c_i)=\prod H_d(c_i)$. Representability gives an object $Rd$ and natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(c,Rd)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(Fc,d)$. For $a:d\to d'$, postcomposition induces a transformation $H_d\to H_{d'}$. Under these bijections it corresponds to a unique map $Ra:Rd\to Rd'$: evaluate the transformation at $Rd$ on its identity, then use naturality to check every component is postcomposition by that map. Uniqueness proves preservation of identity and composition. The same construction makes the bijections natural in $d$, giving $F\dashv R$. This is an ordinary right adjoint for unbounded complexes.
